sourceReview: Read bundled BSB Psalm 85 in full with each verse's related passages before drafting. References are thematic or literary comparisons, not an invented historical occasion. Scripture is never stored in the notes; it loads from the bundled BSB.

study.title: Will You not revive us again?
study.intro: The sons of Korah remember how God once forgave and restored His people, plead with Him to revive them again, and then listen for His answer of peace, where loving devotion, faithfulness, righteousness and peace meet.
study.context: Psalm 85 is headed 'For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah.' It falls into three movements: thanks for past restoration (verses 1-3), a plea for renewal now (verses 4-7), and a prophetic answer of peace and blessing (verses 8-13). Many readers place it after the return from exile, when the people were home again yet still struggling. The psalm teaches that past mercy is the ground for present prayer and future hope.
study.peopleNote: The heading credits the sons of Korah, the Levite family of temple singers, so they are linked. Verse 1 speaks of restoring Jacob, so Jacob is linked. The meeting of mercy and righteousness in verse 10 is fulfilled in Jesus, so He is linked. God is never portrayed as a human body in planned art.

verses.title: Favor shown to the land
verses.heading: Remembering what God has already done
verses.meaning: The psalm begins by looking back: 'You showed favor to Your land, O LORD; You restored Jacob from captivity.' Before asking for anything, the singers recall God's past kindness. 'Restored from captivity' can also be read 'restored the fortunes,' and it likely recalls the return from Babylon. The land is called 'Your land,' a reminder that it belonged to God and that His favor, not their own effort, brought them home.
verses.context: Ezra 1:1-3 records Cyrus allowing the exiles to return and rebuild the house of the LORD. Jeremiah 29:14 had promised, 'I will restore you from captivity.' Psalm 126:1 remembers the return as being like a dream.
explore: Sons of Korah
Levite descendants of Korah who served as temple singers and gatekeepers and wrote several psalms.
Jacob
The patriarch whose name stands for the whole nation of Israel descended from his twelve sons.
verses.reflect: What past kindness from God can you name today as a reason to trust Him with what you need now?
verses.alt: Families with carts and donkeys walk toward green hills at sunrise.

verses.title: Sin covered
verses.heading: Forgiveness that removes the guilt
verses.meaning: Verse 2 names the deepest restoration: 'You forgave the iniquity of Your people; You covered all their sin.' The return to the land meant little without a return to God. To 'forgive' is literally to lift or carry away, and to 'cover' is to hide sin from the judge's sight. The word 'all' matters; nothing was left outstanding. 'Selah' invites a pause to let that sink in before the prayer turns to the present.
verses.context: Psalm 32:1 says, 'Blessed is he whose transgressions are forgiven, whose sins are covered.' Micah 7:18-19 says God casts all our sins into the depths of the sea. Romans 4:7 quotes Psalm 32 to describe righteousness given by faith.
explore: Iniquity
Twisted or crooked wrongdoing, including the guilt that comes with it.
Selah
A musical or liturgical marker of uncertain meaning, often understood as a pause for reflection.
verses.reflect: Is there any sin you still carry as if God had not covered it? What would it mean to believe Him fully?
verses.alt: A heavy sack lies set down beside a path while a figure walks on unburdened.

verses.title: Fury withheld
verses.heading: God turning from burning anger
verses.meaning: Verse 3 completes the memory: 'You withheld all Your fury; You turned from Your burning anger.' God's anger against sin is real and just, and the exile had shown how serious it was. Yet He chose to gather that anger back and turn away from it. The psalm does not pretend sin is harmless; it rejoices that God's mercy has the last word. The same God who judged also relented, and this becomes the basis for the prayer that follows.
verses.context: Exodus 32:14 records that the LORD relented from the disaster He had threatened after Moses prayed. Isaiah 54:8 says, 'In a surge of anger I hid My face from you for a moment, but with everlasting kindness I will have compassion on you.'
explore: Fury
Intense anger; in Scripture God's fury is His settled, just opposition to evil, never a loss of control.
Turned
To turn back or change course; here God turns from executing judgment.
verses.reflect: How does knowing that God's mercy outlasts His anger change the way you approach Him after failing?
verses.alt: Dark storm clouds pull back from a valley as sunlight spreads across fields.

verses.title: Restore us again
verses.heading: Asking God to finish what He started
verses.meaning: Now the psalm turns to present need: 'Restore us, O God of our salvation, and put away Your displeasure toward us.' Though they had been brought home, something was still wrong. Life was hard, and they felt God's displeasure. The same word 'restore' from verse 1 returns; what God did once, they ask Him to do again. Calling Him 'God of our salvation' expresses confidence that rescue belongs to His very character.
verses.context: Haggai 1:6-9 describes returned exiles planting much and harvesting little because God's house lay in ruins. Psalm 80:3 repeats, 'Restore us, O God, and cause Your face to shine upon us.' Lamentations 5:21 prays, 'Restore us to Yourself, O LORD.'
explore: God of our salvation
A title naming God as the source and owner of every rescue His people receive.
Displeasure
Vexation or grief; God's sorrow and frustration with persistent sin.
verses.reflect: Where do you need God to restore you again, even after He has already brought you through once?
verses.alt: Half-rebuilt stone walls stand in a village with workers resting in the shade.

verses.title: Angry forever?
verses.heading: An honest question about how long
verses.meaning: Verse 5 asks two pointed questions: 'Will You be angry with us forever? Will You draw out Your anger to all generations?' The people feared that hardship might stretch on and on, even to their children. These are not accusations but prayers that appeal to what God has revealed about Himself. Scripture allows such honest questions, because they are brought to God rather than away from Him.
verses.context: Psalm 79:5 asks, 'How long, O LORD? Will You be angry forever?' Psalm 103:9 answers, 'He will not always accuse us, nor harbor His anger forever.' Isaiah 57:16 says God will not accuse forever, lest the spirit grow faint.
explore: Generations
Successive families and ages; the fear that judgment would pass from parents to children.
Draw out
To stretch or prolong something, like pulling a cord to its full length.
verses.reflect: What honest question would you like to bring to God, trusting that He is willing to hear it?
verses.alt: A mother and child sit at a doorway looking out over dry fields.

verses.title: Revive us again
verses.heading: New life that leads to joy
verses.meaning: Verse 6 asks with hope: 'Will You not revive us again, that Your people may rejoice in You?' To 'revive' is to give life back to something drooping or near death. The goal is not just relief but joy, and joy 'in You,' that is, joy centered on God Himself. The word 'again' assumes God has done this before and can do it once more. Revival here is the restoration of a people's delight in their God.
verses.context: Habakkuk 3:2 prays, 'Revive them in these years.' Isaiah 57:15 says God dwells with the contrite to revive the spirit of the lowly. Philippians 4:4 urges, 'Rejoice in the Lord always.'
explore: Revive
To make alive again; to restore vigor to what is weak or failing.
Rejoice in You
Gladness whose source and object is God, not only His gifts.
verses.reflect: What would it look like for God to revive your joy in Him this season?
verses.alt: Wilted plants in a garden lift as gentle rain falls on them.

verses.title: Show us loving devotion
verses.heading: Asking to see God's steadfast love
verses.meaning: Verse 7 closes the plea: 'Show us Your loving devotion, O LORD, and grant us Your salvation.' 'Loving devotion' translates hesed, God's loyal, covenant love that never gives up on His people. They ask to see it, to experience it in visible ways. And they ask for salvation, rescue from their present troubles. The prayer rests not on their worthiness but on the kind of God He has promised to be.
verses.context: Exodus 34:6 describes the LORD as 'abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness.' Lamentations 3:22 says, 'Because of the loving devotion of the LORD we are not consumed.' Ephesians 2:4-5 says God, rich in mercy, made us alive with Christ.
explore: Loving devotion
The Hebrew hesed: loyal, steadfast covenant love that keeps its promises.
Salvation
Rescue or deliverance from danger, distress or sin, given by God.
verses.reflect: Where have you seen God's loyal love lately, and where do you long to see it more clearly?
verses.alt: A family gathers around a lamp in a small stone house at dusk.

verses.title: Listening for peace
verses.heading: Waiting to hear God speak
verses.meaning: In verse 8 the singer stops asking and starts listening: 'I will listen to what God the LORD will say; for He will surely speak peace to His people and His saints.' Prayer is not only talking; it includes waiting for God's word. The expected answer is peace, shalom, wholeness and well-being. A warning follows: 'He will not let them return to folly.' God's peace includes turning His people away from the foolishness that brought trouble before.
verses.context: 1 Samuel 3:10 records Samuel saying, 'Speak, for Your servant is listening.' Isaiah 26:3 promises perfect peace to the one whose mind is steadfast. John 14:27 records Jesus saying, 'Peace I leave with you; My peace I give you.'
explore: Peace
The Hebrew shalom: wholeness, completeness and right relationship with God and others.
Folly
Moral foolishness; choosing ways that ignore God and lead to harm.
verses.reflect: How can you make room to listen to God through His Word today rather than only speaking to Him?
verses.alt: A shepherd sits quietly on a hillside at dawn, head bowed, listening.

verses.title: Salvation is near
verses.heading: Glory dwelling in the land
verses.meaning: Verse 9 states the promise: 'Surely His salvation is near to those who fear Him, that His glory may dwell in our land.' Those who 'fear' God, who revere and trust Him, will find rescue close at hand. The aim is that God's glory, His weighty and radiant presence, may live among them again. After exile, when the glory had seemed to depart, this was a precious hope. Christians hear in it a pointer to God coming to dwell with His people in person.
verses.context: Ezekiel 43:2-5 describes the glory of the God of Israel returning to fill the temple. John 1:14 says the Word became flesh and 'we have seen His glory.' Haggai 2:9 promises the latter glory of the house will be greater than the former.
explore: Fear Him
Reverent awe and trust toward God that shapes how a person lives.
Glory
The weight and splendor of God's presence made known among people.
verses.reflect: Where do you long to see God's presence and glory made real in your home or community?
verses.alt: Golden morning light rests over a hilltop town and its terraced fields.

verses.title: Love and faithfulness meet
verses.heading: Righteousness and peace kiss
verses.meaning: Verse 10 is one of the most beautiful lines in the Psalms: 'Loving devotion and faithfulness have joined together; righteousness and peace have kissed.' Qualities that might seem to pull apart, mercy and truth, justice and peace, come together in perfect harmony. God does not sacrifice holiness to show kindness. Christians have long seen this meeting fulfilled at the cross, where God's justice and His love were both fully shown.
verses.context: Romans 3:26 says God is both just and the one who justifies those who have faith in Jesus. Psalm 89:14 says righteousness and justice are the foundation of God's throne, and loving devotion and faithfulness go before Him. Ephesians 2:14 calls Christ our peace.
explore: Faithfulness
Firm reliability; God's truthfulness in keeping every word He speaks.
Righteousness
Rightness according to God's own standard; doing what is just and true.
verses.reflect: Do you tend to see God as mostly loving or mostly just? How does this verse hold both together for you?
verses.alt: Two streams flow together into one clear pool among rocks.

verses.title: From earth and heaven
verses.heading: Faithfulness sprouts, righteousness looks down
verses.meaning: Verse 11 pictures blessing moving in two directions: 'Faithfulness sprouts from the earth, and righteousness looks down from heaven.' Truth grows up from the ground like a plant, while God's righteousness leans down from above. Earth and heaven are joined. When God restores His people, faithfulness springs up in their lives in answer to the righteousness He sends. It is an image of harmony between God and His people, and between heaven and earth.
verses.context: Isaiah 45:8 says, 'Drip down, O heavens, from above... let the earth open up that salvation may sprout.' Isaiah 61:11 compares God's righteousness to a garden making seeds sprout. Matthew 6:10 prays, 'Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.'
explore: Sprouts
To spring up or grow, like a shoot breaking through soil.
Looks down
To lean over and gaze from above, as from a window.
verses.reflect: Where would you like to see faithfulness sprout in your own life this week?
verses.alt: Green shoots rise from plowed earth under a bright open sky.

verses.title: The land yields
verses.heading: God gives what is good
verses.meaning: Verse 12 makes the promise practical: 'The LORD will indeed provide what is good, and our land will yield its increase.' After hard years of poor harvests, the people are assured that God will give good things, including crops. Spiritual renewal and physical blessing are linked under the old covenant. The deeper point is that all good comes from God's hand, whether grain in the field or grace in the heart.
verses.context: Leviticus 26:4 promises rain in season so that the land will yield its produce. James 1:17 says every good and perfect gift is from above. Psalm 67:6 says, 'The earth has yielded its harvest; God, our God, blesses us.'
explore: Increase
The produce or harvest that the land brings forth each season.
Provide what is good
To give good gifts; God supplying what truly benefits His people.
verses.reflect: What good gifts from God, large or small, can you thank Him for today?
verses.alt: Farmers carry baskets of grain from a golden field at harvest.

verses.title: Preparing His steps
verses.heading: Righteousness goes ahead of God
verses.meaning: The psalm ends with a picture of God on the move: 'Righteousness will go before Him to prepare the way for His steps.' Like a herald clearing a road for a king, righteousness marches ahead of the LORD. Where God comes, He brings rightness with Him and makes a path for His people to follow. The promise of restoration ends not with the people settling down but with God Himself coming near.
verses.context: Isaiah 40:3 calls, 'Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness.' Mark 1:2-3 applies this to John the Baptist preparing the way for Jesus. Psalm 89:14 says loving devotion and faithfulness go before God.
explore: Go before
To walk ahead as a herald or forerunner, announcing who is coming.
Steps
Footsteps or path; the way God walks among His people.
verses.reflect: How might God want to prepare a path in your life so you can walk in step with Him?
verses.alt: A cleared road winds through the hills toward a distant sunrise.
